title: Breathing difficulty or asthma attack
summary: Allow a comfortable position, help with the person’s prescribed reliever, and recognize severe breathing failure.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Asthma
WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
actions: If smoke, gas, or another hazard is present, do not enter an unsafe area. Move to fresh air only when it is safe and call emergency services.
Let an alert person sit in the position that makes breathing easiest, often upright and leaning slightly forward. Loosen tight clothing.
Help the person use their own prescribed reliever inhaler according to their action plan or device instructions.
Call emergency services immediately for inability to speak a full sentence, blue or grey lips, confusion, drowsiness, very little air movement, or no rapid improvement with the reliever.
Stay with the person and monitor breathing. Start CPR if breathing becomes absent or abnormal.
prohibitions: Do not give another person’s medicine.
Do not force an alert breathless person to lie flat, walk, or exercise.
Do not delay emergency help when severe signs are present.

redFlags.text: Emergency warning signs selected—contact emergency services now.

emergencyCall.text: Blue or grey lips, confusion, drowsiness, or inability to speak in full sentences requires immediate emergency help.
